_meta.indication: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older (original 2020 approval).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial; patients randomized 1:1:1 to berotralstat 110 mg, 150 mg, or placebo once daily for a 24-week treatment period.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent patients 12 years of age and older with type I or II HAE who experienced at least two investigator-confirmed attacks within the first 8 weeks of the run-in period; median baseline attack rate 2.9/month.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Rate of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks during dosing throughout the 24-week treatment period (expressed as attacks per 28 days).
pivotal_trials.n: 120 randomized (110 mg n=41, 150 mg n=40, placebo n=40)
pivotal_trials.result: Met primary endpoint for both doses: estimated attack rate 1.65 (110 mg) and 1.31 (150 mg) vs 2.35 (placebo) per 28 days; rate reduction 30.0% (p=0.024) and 44.2% (p<0.001) relative to placebo.

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety Study of BCX7353 as an Oral Treatment for the Prevention of Attacks in HAE

key_safety: Main safety signals were gastrointestinal-related adverse reactions and transaminase elevations. Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): abdominal pain (110 mg 10%, 150 mg 23%), vomiting (10%, 15%), diarrhea (10%, 15%), back pain (2%, 10%), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (10%, 5%); GI reactions were more frequent with 150 mg.
target_moa: Berotralstat is an orally administered inhibitor of active plasma kallikrein; it decreases vascular permeability and edema by reducing bradykinin, which is produced when kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen.
modality: Small molecule (orally administered plasma kallikrein inhibitor)

rems.type: A REMS will not be required; labeling adequately conveys the safety risks.

advisory_committee.vote: The Pulmonary and Allergy Drug Advisory Committee (PADAC) was not convened; no significant or unexpected safety or efficacy issues were raised.

orphan_indication.text: Berotralstat was granted orphan (therapy) designation on November 1, 2017 for HAE, which is categorized as an orphan disease.

citations.quote: Berotralstat was granted orphan therapy designation on November 1, 2017, and fast-track designation on August 2, 2018.

Although the exact prevalence is unknown, HAE is estimated to affect 1 in 10,000 to 50,000 individuals worldwide (approximately 6,000 to 10,000 individuals in the United States) and is categorized as an orphan disease.
Berotralstat has been granted orphan drug designation and is exempt from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act.

summary.text: Original 505(b)(1) NDA submitted by BioCryst on December 3, 2019 and reviewed under Standard review; berotralstat had orphan drug designation (Nov 1, 2017) and fast-track designation (Aug 2, 2018) and was approved December 3, 2020 based on a single pivotal Phase 3 trial (Study 302). No accelerated approval, breakthrough, or priority review; no advisory committee.

citations.quote: This is an original (505(b)(1)) NDA submitted by the applicant, BioCryst Pharmaceuticals (BioCryst), on December 3, 2019, seeking marketing approval for ORLADEYO (berotralstat), an orally administered plasma kallikrein inhibitor indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in patients 12 years of age and older.
Berotralstat was granted orphan therapy designation on November 1, 2017, and fast-track designation on August 2, 2018.
